_comment: Which rail each capacitor sits on, and what that rail runs at.
The rated voltage is NOT here -- it is read from the parts list at run time,
so a corrected BOM corrects this too.
A4 has six capacitors and only two of them belong in a recap audit. Recap
ranks tantalums by voltage margin and aluminiums by capacitance lost; the
other four here are a ceramic (C2, 1000 pF), a polyester (C3, 0.1 uF), a
line-rated polyester (C5, 0.1 uF 250 V ac) and a second ceramic (C6,
6800 pF), none of which is an electrolytic and none of which ages the way
this mode is looking for. There is not a single aluminium can on the board.
So this file audits two parts, and that is the whole population rather than
a sample -- which is worth saying outright, because an audit file with two
entries otherwise looks like unfinished work.
Both entries were traced on schematic sheet 3, and the trace is the reason
they are worth recording at all: C1 and C4 are 35 V tantalums sitting at
24 V, which is 69% of rating. That is the highest margin ratio on this
assembly by a long way and it is not an error -- it is what the circuit is.
Each fan runs from +12V FAN to -12V FAN, 24 V across it, and C1 and C4 are
connected across that pair ahead of the sense resistors R2 and R3, not from
one rail to common. A reading of 12 V here would be the easy mistake and it
would understate the stress by half.
source is used strictly:
'schematic'  the net was traced on the sheet AND the manuals state what
that net runs at. Both entries qualify: sheet 3 draws the
connection and Table 2-2 gives A19's +12 V and -12 V outputs.
railClass is how much energy is behind the rail, which decides what a
shorted part does. This board's one letter:
B  the output of a three-terminal IC regulator, one rail either side --
A19's U1 (7812) and U2 (7912), each current limited and thermally
protected, reaching this board through J41 with no local reservoir
anywhere on A4. A short here is survivable and presents as both fans
stopping rather than as damage.
Hand-authored; tools/import_cap_audit.py was not used.

C1.net: +12V FAN to -12V FAN (across fan 1, ahead of R2)
C1.note: 10 uF 35 V tantalum, polarity marked + on the +12V FAN side. Sheet 3 shows it connected between the +12V FAN line and the -12V FAN line on the supply side of the 2 ohm sense resistor R2, so it sees the whole 24 V the fan runs on rather than one 12 V rail. 24 V on a 35 V part is 69% of rating -- high for a solid tantalum by modern practice, normal for 1987, and comfortably the most stressed capacitor on this assembly. Both rails come from A19's U1 and U2 through J41 pins 20A/20C and 27A/27C; Table 2-2 gives them as +12 V and -12 V.

C4.net: +12V FAN to -12V FAN (across fan 2, ahead of R3)
C4.note: The twin of C1 on the fan 2 circuit, identical part in an identical position: across the same +12V FAN / -12V FAN pair, on the supply side of R3. Same 24 V, same 69% of a 35 V rating. If one of the two has failed the other has had the same service life at the same stress, so replace them as a pair.
